title: ITV investigating Coronation Street actor Jacob Roberts after bar incident

input.lead: Police say they attended a Manchester bar after reports of a disturbance earlier this month
input.summary: Police say they attended a Manchester bar after reports of a disturbance earlier this month
input.evidence_text: ITV investigating Coronation Street actor Jacob Roberts after bar incident - BBC News Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Jacob Roberts has starred in Coronation Street since 2024 By Miriam Barker North West Published 22 November 2026 ITV is investigating a Coronation Street actor following an alleged bar altercation. Jacob Roberts is known for playing Det Con Kit Green on the ITV soap since 2024. According to reports by the Sun newspaper, video footage appears to show him shouting outside Kiely's Irish Bar in Manchester on 8 November. Greater Manchester Police said officers had attended a bar in Watson Street at about 02:30 GMT following reports of a disturbance. No arrests have been made. An ITV spokesperson said they were investigating and would be speaking with Roberts. Roberts was allegedly trying to get into the bar, with staff claiming he was acting aggressively and swearing when he was told he could not come in as the venue was closing. Roberts previously played Damon Kinsella on the Channel 4 soap Hollyoaks from 2017 until 2023, before joining the cobbles in 2024. He has also appeared in Emmerdale and recently starred in the crossover episode Corridale. His storylines on Coronation Street include being diagnosed with male breast cancer as well as fathering a child after an illicit affair with his girlfriend's daughter. Roberts' representatives have been contacted for comment. It included an order that "food is prepared in a way that prevents choking and children are within sight and hearing of staff". Denton Daycare Ltd later decided to permanently close, citing the company's "financial challenges". The watchdog report revealed inspectors also told the nursery to ensure proper hand washing routines were implemented, install better safeguarding procedures and give all children daily access to outdoor play. Arrangements for children with special educational needs and disabilities were also criticised. Denton Daycare Ltd company director Alina Naveed apologised to parents for the "difficult circumstances" they are facing having to find alternative childcare at such short notice - as well as staff. Keeley's three-year-old son was one of the nursery's children and she told the Local Democracy Reporting Service reading the Ofsted letter "left me feeling quite shocked" at the "sheer number and seriousness of the failures identified". "You expect [your child] to be safe, cared for and supported, and some of the things highlighted in that letter are really difficult to read," she added. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Entry-level recruitment has become more difficult, with employers increasingly favouring experienced candidates and many graduates and other new entrants struggling to secure their fi Manchester Digital contributed to the development of the plan through its involvement in the government's Digital Skills Council, drawing on its work with employers and education providers across Greater Manchester Around 800,000 digital and technology roles are projected to need filling over the next decade.
